notes.text: OpenAI shipped GPT-5.4 (5 Mar), GPT-5.5 (24 Apr), the GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna family (9 Jul), GPT-6 Astra (3 Sep), GPT-6 Sol and Luna (22 Sep) and GPT-6.1 Sol (29 Sep). The Assistants API shut down on 26 Aug 2026 and self-serve fine-tuning is being wound down.

Current Claude line-up: Fable 5.1 (1 Sep), Opus 5.5 (22 Sep), Sonnet 5.5 (28 Sep), Haiku 5.5 (7 Oct). Haiku 4.5 is now 'Legacy'; Sonnet 4.5 was deprecated on 30 Sep 2026 with retirement on 30 Nov 2026. Legacy still available: Fable 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.8, 4.7, 4.6. Claude Mythos 5 / 5.1 exist with limited availability.

Gemini 3.1 Pro (preview, Feb), 3.5 Flash-Lite and 3.6 Flash (21 Jul), 3.7 Flash (13 Aug), 3.8 Flash (2 Sep). Gemini 4 Argon announced 30 Sep 2026, first to trusted cyber defenders, at an introductory $2/$10.

Grok 4.7 (21 Sep), DeepSeek V4 (24 Apr) then V4.1 Flash (10 Sep), Mistral Large 4 preview (6 Oct, 1.05T MoE announced as open-weight, weights 'coming soon'), Meta's proprietary Muse Spark line (1.1 to 1.3), Kimi K3 (2.8T parameters, open weights), GLM-5.3, Qwen3.8-Max, MiniMax-M3, Cohere Command A+ (open weights, May 2026) and TypeSafe's Jev decision model in early access.

The most capable cyber-relevant models are released in stages: Claude Mythos (limited availability), OpenAI's Daybreak programme (GPT-5.6 Cyber, approval required), Google's Gemini 4 Argon via the Fairwind Program. An SME cannot buy these off the shelf today.

notes.topic: Price trend: new flagships cost less or the same
notes.text: Claude Opus 5.5 is $4/$20 vs $5/$25 for Opus 5; Sonnet 5's $2/$10 launch price became permanent; Claude Haiku 5.5 ($0.10/$0.50 up to 100k-token prompts) is 10x cheaper per token than Haiku 4.5 ($1/$5) and Sonnet 5.5 cache reads were halved to $0.10 (both 7 Oct); GPT-6.1 Sol ($2/$10) is sold as near-Astra at a fifth of Astra's $10/$50; GPT-5.6 Luna cut 80% and Terra 20% on 30 Jul; GPT-5.6 Sol cut on 21 Aug; DeepSeek cut prices with V4.1 Flash; MiniMax-M3 'permanent 50% off'.

Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.7/3.6 Flash prices double on 1 Jan 2027 ($0.75/$3.75 to $1.50/$7.50). OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI and Mistral all charge about +10% for regional (data residency) processing. Long prompts cost more at OpenAI (>272K: 2x input, 1.5x output), Google (>200K), xAI (>=200K), MiniMax (>512K) and now Claude Haiku 5.5 (>100K: 5x); Anthropic's other models and Meta charge no long-context premium.

Off-peak pricing (DeepSeek, half price outside peak UTC hours), cache-write charges (OpenAI GPT-6 at 1.25x input, Anthropic, Kimi K3), 'Fast'/'Ultrafast' premium tiers, and training-for-discount tiers (Meta Muse Spark Contributor at $0.10/$0.20 in exchange for training on your data).

The strongest open-weight models on Artificial Analysis's leaderboard are Chinese (8 Oct 2026): MiMo-V2.6-Pro 46, GLM-5.3 45, Kimi K3 44, GLM-5.3-Flash 42, Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B 40, versus 12 for gpt-oss-120b; AA lists Qwen3.8 Max (0902, 45) and Mistral Large 4 Preview (38) as not open weights. Top closed models score 52-58 (Claude Opus 5.5 at 58). They are also cheap: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash $0.30/$1.20 peak, GLM-5.3-Flash $0.15/$0.50. Licences vary (MIT for DeepSeek and GLM-5.3-Flash, custom licences for Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, MiniMax-M3).

Mistral's EU platform sells Z.ai GLM 5.3 ($1.4/$4.4), and Alibaba lists Germany (Frankfurt), Global scope, for Qwen3.8-Max ($1.65/$4.951) and Qwen3.8-Flash ($0.113/$0.382), so some Chinese models can be used without sending data to China. None of DeepSeek, Alibaba, Moonshot, Zhipu or MiniMax appears on the EU GPAI Code of Practice signatory list.

Mistral AI (France) is the main European model vendor: Large 4 (preview, announced open-weight with weights 'coming soon', $0.68/$2.09 launch price), Medium 3.5 (open weights, Modified MIT), Small 4 (Apache 2.0), Ministral 3 (Apache 2.0), with an EU inference endpoint. Other European entries on the Artificial Analysis leaderboard: Multiverse Computing's Quasar 438B. EU-based signatories of the GPAI code include Aleph Alpha, Mistral, Black Forest Labs, LINAGORA, Pleias, Almawave, Fastweb, Domyn, Dweve.

Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models apply since 2 Aug 2025; the Commission's enforcement powers, including fines, apply from 2 Aug 2026; models placed on the market before 2 Aug 2025 must comply by 2 Aug 2027. These obligations fall on the model provider, not on the SME that uses the model.

Meta and the Chinese labs are absent from the list.

notes.topic: AI Act: what applies to SMEs as deployers
notes.text: The Act became applicable on 2 Aug 2026; AI literacy obligations and prohibited practices apply since 2 Feb 2025; transparency rules from Aug 2026; high-risk use cases (e.g. employment, education) from 2 Dec 2027 and AI in regulated products from 2 Aug 2028 after the 'AI Omnibus' simplification (proposal adopted 19 November 2025, political agreement 7 May 2026, in force since 27 July 2026); a ninth prohibition takes effect in Dec 2026.

EU processing is available first-party from OpenAI (Enterprise / approved API projects, eu.api.openai.com) and Mistral (api.eu.mistral.ai); Anthropic's first-party API offers only global or US, so EU processing for Claude goes through Amazon Bedrock EU geo inference (Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Haiku 4.5; not Fable 5.1) or Google Cloud's EU multi-region; xAI offers only global or US.

Team seats now cluster at $20/user/month annual (ChatGPT Business, Claude Team standard, Claude Enterprise base seat) with $100 'premium' seats for 5x usage at both OpenAI and Anthropic; Claude Team now adds up to $500 a month of pooled API credits; Microsoft 365 Copilot Business add-on $21 (promo $18) and enterprise $30; Perplexity Enterprise Pro $34; Mistral Team $24.99 (same figure in EUR). Google Workspace Business Standard is EUR 13.60 per user per month from France.
